A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BiSSL framework. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and matchable despite substantial reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v3 reports original classification and object-detection experiments, pretraining-duration comparisons and latent-feature visualizations.

after.justification: v4 retains those original results and adds ablations, alternative-baseline comparisons, MAE experiments, dataset-size tests, ImageNet fine-tuning and computation-time measurements.

M1.justification: The BiSSL objectives, regularizer and alternating optimization procedure are retained. However, Algorithm 2 changes y = v + g/(lambda + lambda_damp) to an expression using y instead of g before y is defined. This is an apparently erroneous revision to the documented computation; the PDFs do not establish an implemented redesign.

E1.justification: v4 adds masked-reconstruction pretraining through MAE and labeled ImageNet classification as a downstream task. The twelve existing transfer-classification datasets, VOC detection and STL10 pretraining remain. Coverage expands within the existing image domain; varying Pets sample counts does not introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: Appendix C.5 adds evaluated comparisons against weighted joint optimization of pretext and downstream losses and against NoisyTune on Pets, DTD, VOC07 and Flowers. v3 compared against conventional fine-tuning only. NoisyTune was already cited in v3, but was not an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: New protocols include MAE with a ViT-S backbone, 8-by-8 patches and AdamW; upper-level iteration ablations with T = 500 or 4000; Pets subsets containing 5–75 samples per class; and ImageNet fine-tuning with 1%, 10% and 100% labels, 50 epochs and T = 100. Appendix experiments also introduce smaller hyperparameter-search budgets. The retained main experimental settings and Tables 3–5 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 adds tests of multiple upper-level updates and removal of the first upper-level loss term in C.3, weighting sensitivity for joint optimization in C.5, sample-size sensitivity in C.6, and the aligned-distribution setting in C.7. These substantially expand investigation of design choices and applicability beyond the retained pretraining-duration analysis and feature visualizations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten models trained with different random seeds and report means and standard deviations, with selected comparisons marked significant in bold. The new result tables continue this reporting style without introducing a changed run-count policy, confidence intervals or a specified new significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–2 and the top-5 results in v3 Table 6/v4 Table 7 are unchanged. v4 adds substantial results in Tables 6 and 8–13, including MAE Flowers accuracy of 87.2 versus 81.1 for Only FT, and ImageNet improvements of 2.1, 0.2 and 0.0 percentage points at the three label fractions. These are newly reported comparisons. A repeated DTD default entry also reports standard deviation 0.4 in Tables 8 and 11, versus 0.3 in retained Table 1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 introduces Theorem 1 and a proof arguing for the necessity of the second upper-level loss term. The existing implicit-derivative derivation moves to A.2 and is substantially retained. The new proof has a sign error: Equation 12 differentiates the quadratic penalty using theta_D minus theta_P instead of theta_P minus theta_D, invalidating the displayed stationary-point construction as written.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a task-agnostic intermediate bilevel training stage that improves pretraining/downstream alignment and performance on most of twelve classification datasets and on object detection. The rewritten abstract and conclusion invoke additional investigative evidence without materially redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.2 changes the second loss term's rationale from empirical stabilization and being nonessential to claimed structural necessity. New C.7 and Appendix D qualify benefits when pretraining and downstream distributions align, and explicitly identify requirements for pretext data, pretext heads and matching backbone architectures. Added analyses also interpret the roles of upper-level updates and bilevel coupling.

D1.justification: v4 substantially expands implementation and resource reporting: A100/A40 hardware, GPU-hour measurements, MAE optimization settings, weighted-baseline implementation, NoisyTune's 0.015 noise scale, and additional search budgets. These include disclosures about retained experiments, not evidence that their hardware changed. The stated code/model-weight repository target also changes, while existing hyperparameter Tables 3–5 are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds references 75–78 covering data-efficient transformers, transformer spatial design, AdamW and LoRA. The main positioning against earlier bilevel SSL and backbone-priming approaches remains substantially unchanged. MAE and NoisyTune were already cited in v3.

P1.justification: The abstract, portions of the introduction, training-pipeline explanation, pretraining-duration discussion, feature-analysis narrative and conclusion are rewritten. The appendices are reorganized around expanded analyses and a dedicated limitations section. Terminology changes from implicit gradient to implicit Jacobian, alongside title, front-matter and citation-style edits.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the two-column main-text layout with a single-column format, revises Figure 1 and its caption, numbers algorithm lines, and changes plot colors and axis labels. Figure 3's feature panels become vertically stacked. Seven new tables are added; existing tables and feature visualizations are resized or relocated rather than replaced by new evidence.

improvement.justification: The MAE evaluation, alternative-baseline comparisons and component ablations address gaps in v3's support for broad applicability and the value of bilevel optimization. Explicit applicability limits further improve transparency. However, the new theorem's sign error and Algorithm 2's undefined self-reference weaken mathematical reliability and reproducibility. The added evidence supports a limited net improvement, tempered by these technical defects.
